solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: How clergyman may be seen making careful purchases?

definitions.meaning: a priest is seen dressed in his robes
the act of putting money into assets in the hope of a return

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a vicar might be spotted while prudently shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word as IN VESTMENT: a clergyman is seen wearing his robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Investing is the business of buying assets carefully with an eye to future gain.

clue.text: Teacher training — no English this month

indicators.note: no signals that the following letter is dropped from the word before

parts.note: INSET is in-service training for teachers in British schools

explanation.surface: A note that staff training days have no English sessions scheduled this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INSET days are British school days set aside for in-service teacher training; 'no' removes the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Inst. is the old letter-writing abbreviation for instant, meaning of the current month.

clue.text: Vice-President's operations steer constrained expressions of opinion

indicators.note: constrained means held in, so one piece is enclosed by the others

parts.note: VP is the usual abbreviation for Vice-President
a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
OPS is short for operations, as in military ops

explanation.surface: A deputy leader's staff are steered into giving only limited statements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steer' looks like a verb but is the animal; 'constrained' means held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vox pops are street interviews gathering the opinions of passers-by, from Latin for voice of the people.

clue.text: Set over? Fantastic, I'm ready for my close-up!

parts.note: super is a casual word for fantastic
I'm written without its apostrophe gives IM
an actor ready for a close-up shot has struck a pose, so is posed

explanation.surface: A film star gushes before the camera, echoing Norma Desmond's line in Sunset Boulevard.
explanation.definitionFit: To superimpose an image is to lay it over another one.

clue.text: Festive delicacy 'name' cook turned out

indicators.note: turned out suggests letters reshaped into something else

explanation.surface: A dish named after the chef who produced it for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges NAME and COOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooncakes are rich pastries eaten at the Chinese Mid-Autumn Festival.

clue.text: Born and died with no ego found necessary

parts.note: née, French for born, introduces a maiden name

indicators.note: with no tells us to leave out the next piece

parts.note: died as written
ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: A selfless life summed up: born, died, never thinking of self.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' takes I out of DIED, giving DED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needed is something that was found to be required or necessary.

clue.text: Get one over D Cameron's partner (better half?)

indicators.note: better half here means keep the front half of the name, the question mark flagging the pun on a wife

parts.note: the former UK prime minister's wife Samantha, written in the same style as D Cameron, is S Cameron

explanation.surface: A tease about whether the prime minister's wife is really the better half of the couple.
explanation.walkthrough: Write Samantha Cameron the way the clue writes David's name, initial plus surname, and keep the first four of its eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To scam someone is to swindle or trick them, putting one over on them.

clue.text: Knot where cavalry commander's besieged Lakota leader

indicators.note: besieged means surrounded, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: General Custer led the US 7th Cavalry at Little Bighorn

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A battlefield scene at Little Bighorn, where Custer fought the Lakota.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface the Lakota surrounded Custer; in the wordplay the roles flip and CUSTER surrounds L.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot can mean a tight group of people or things, a cluster.

clue.text: Cream cheese ace after mum's fish

indicators.note: after places the piece mentioned first behind the others

parts.note: ma is another word for mum, so mum's gives MA'S
a carp is a freshwater fish
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A boast that a cheese is excellent when served after mother's fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascarpone is a soft Italian cheese made from cream.

clue.text: Brassy types reported to have bagged mobiles?

indicators.note: reported tells us the answer sounds like the phrase

parts.note: to have bagged mobiles is to have sacks of phones, said casually as sacks o' phones

explanation.surface: Bold people rumoured to have pocketed a load of mobile phones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brassy' looks like brash, but it means made of brass.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxophones are made of brass, though classed as woodwind because of their reed.

clue.text: Projects simply needing time brought forward

indicators.note: brought forward means moved earlier, so the letter shifts towards the front

parts.note: just means simply or merely

explanation.surface: Talk of schemes whose only need is an earlier deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought forward' moves the T of JUST one place forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to stick out, as a ledge juts out.

clue.text: Underground seams not worked here, as pitmen once worked

indicators.note: worked means shaped or manipulated, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A mining remark about coal being dug the old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' in its second appearance rearranges AS PITMEN ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An opencast mine extracts coal from the surface, not by tunnelling.

clue.text: Tough stuff from company tax inspectors

parts.note: IR stands for Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority

explanation.surface: A business getting a hard time from the taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was Britain's tax collector before HMRC.
explanation.definitionFit: Coir is the strong, coarse fibre from coconut husks, used for matting and rope.

clue.text: Queen cat biting big cat (Manx) biting first cat's tail

indicators.note: the second biting has the trimmed big cat seize a letter from the first cat
biting means taking in with the jaws, so one piece holds another

parts.note: cat as written

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a leopard is a big cat

indicators.note: tail points to the final letter of the first cat mentioned

explanation.surface: A cat fight: a queen cat, a tailless Manx and a big cat all biting each other.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manx cat has no tail, so 'Manx' docks the big cat's last letter. The second 'biting' moves the first cat's T into LEOPAR, giving C-LEOPA(T)R-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling queen of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Ramp up Libor dishonestly — caught exaggerating

parts.note: to hype is to ramp up or talk up

indicators.note: dishonestly suggests the letters have been fiddled into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Bankers fraudulently push up the Libor interest rate and are caught.
explanation.walkthrough: Libor is the London interbank lending rate, famously rigged by traders; 'dishonestly' rearranges it to RBOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbole is exaggeration, so hyperbolic language is overstating things.

clue.text: Do they mask a shy disposition?

definitions.text: Do they mask a shy disposition?

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so these letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A question whether veils hide a timid nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' means arrangement, rearranging MASK A SHY; the whole clue also describes the veil.
explanation.definitionFit: Yashmaks are veils worn by some Muslim women, covering the face in public.

clue.text: Open war breaks out between multinational force and Portugal

indicators.note: between places a piece in the middle of two others

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, deploys multinational peacekeeping forces
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

indicators.note: breaks out suggests the letters burst into new order

explanation.surface: A news report of fighting erupting between UN peacekeepers and Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks out' is the anagram signal, not part of the war story; 'between' sets the result in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwrap a parcel is to open it.

clue.text: Nightcap's a knockout with rum in

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hotty, or hottie, is a stunningly attractive person, a knockout
rum means strange or odd

explanation.surface: A bedtime drink that packs a punch thanks to the rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the spirit in the drink but means odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a drink taken before bed, such as whisky with hot water and honey.

clue.text: One who has issues to deal with rioted violently

definitions.text: One who has issues to deal with

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone with personal problems who ran riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issues' suggests personal problems; here they are editions of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is responsible for preparing each issue of a publication.

clue.text: Where legal lunch will be shortly

definitions.meaning: a lawyer's packed lunch would go in the briefcase, read as inside a legal brief
in short, briefly, to sum up

explanation.definitionFit: Briefly or in summary is the usual meaning of the phrase, from a short statement.

clue.text: Sellers perhaps accepting other side may get to cancel

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: Peter Sellers was one of the Goons of the BBC radio comedy The Goon Show
the back is the other side from the front

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers who take returns may be able to cancel a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sellers' looks like traders; it is the comedian Peter Sellers, a member of the Goons.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back on a promise is to renege on or cancel it.

clue.text: 'Wow, heavy!' said Arabian

indicators.note: said tells us the answer sounds like the words

parts.note: an exclamation of surprise at a heavy weight could be coo, weighty

explanation.surface: An Arab exclaiming at how heavy something is.
explanation.walkthrough: COO, WEIGHTY spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuwait lies on the Arabian Peninsula, so someone from there is an Arabian.

clue.text: Sustained six and four, then unfortunately out

parts.note: six plus four makes ten

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters fall out badly into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket innings: a six and a four, then the batter is unluckily out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sustained' is a musical direction; 'unfortunately' rearranges OUT to UTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenuto is the musical instruction to hold a note for its full value.

clue.text: Southern area of Christian restraint?

definitions.meaning: a region of the southern US with strong evangelical Protestant influence
a strap holding in a Christian, a belt made of scripture

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible Belt is the conservative evangelical region across the American South.

clue.text: Drag queen's ultimate alternative to gown

parts.note: to drag is to tow or haul

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so the last letter is used

explanation.surface: A drag queen choosing between a gown and something else to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag queen' splits into two pieces. Town and gown are the townspeople and the university in Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The old phrase town and gown contrasts local residents with the university community.

clue.text: What makes best basest, say

definitions.meaning: putting AS inside the word best turns it into basest

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to introduce an example, like saying for instance.

clue.text: Cut of buffalo intestine

indicators.note: of suggests taking a piece out of the following words

explanation.surface: A butcher describing a piece of buffalo offal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'buffalo' and the start of 'intestine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is a cut of meat taken from the back of an animal.

clue.text: Wizard fun skipping church, and essence of priests' quibbles

indicators.note: skipping means missing out, so a piece is removed

parts.note: Quidditch is the flying broomstick game played by wizards in the Harry Potter books

indicators.note: the essence is the heart, so the central letters are taken

explanation.surface: Priests quibbling over a wizard game and churchgoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipping' drops CH from QUIDDITCH, and 'essence of' takes the central IES of PRIESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiddity is a trivial objection or hair-splitting distinction, a quibble.

clue.text: Box that should be kept at arm's length?

definitions.meaning: box means hit, as with a blow

definitions.text: that should be kept at arm's length?
definitions.meaning: a shirt ... sits at the end of the arm

explanation.definitionFit: To cuff is to hit with an open hand, and a cuff is the end of a sleeve.

clue.text: One of people scattered on any isle (or on specific ones)

definitions.text: One of people scattered on any isle (or on specific ones)

indicators.note: one of means a single letter from the word, here its first
scattered suggests the letters are spread into new order

explanation.surface: Describing islanders spread over many Pacific islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges ON ANY ISLE after P; the whole describes the islanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesians are the peoples spread across the many islands of the central and south Pacific.
